Debbie Els

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Online Money scams are nothing new, but Debbie Els has been living off Good Samaritan-donations for many years!

Unique Selling Point:
Debbie Els is a colourful character. When the farmers marched on Senekal, she was in the front line to support them, when parents cordoned off the Brackenfell High School in Cape Town to defend it against EFF protesters, Debbie went live on social media and claimed that she was under attack. She was nowhere near the incident. She picked a fight with the Cape Town Police when they arrested bathers during the Covid lockdown. She claimed afterwards that she was severely beaten and even broke her back in two places. “Rubbish”, says those who know her, “there is nothing wrong, She just loves the limelight”.

Summary:
The name, Debbie Els is linked to numerous Facebook groups raising funds for worthy causes -- they include the Million March and I’m Staying, The plight of Farmers in SA, Anti-Vaxx... you name it. She adopts a cause and proceeds to raise funds via various FB groups.. But the money never gets to the beneficiaries... it ends up in her pocket or spent on unrelated expenses.

Els has been in jail twice - for selling properties that did not belong to her, and for illegally marrying a man in Mauritius whilst still legally married to her husband in SA. She has been agent to the stars, arranged concerts and never paying artists and ... She even dated a young up-and-coming Afrikaans artist, but when things turned sour she accused him of rape and child abuse... The cases against him were dropped.

Debbie then set her sights on Farm Murders and decided that she would make a movie to highlight the plight of white farmers under attack in SA. She got a script from a young man and never paid him. Then she raised funds to go sell the idea in Hollywood, and although she did go to the USA, there never was a movie and she ended up having nothing more than a holiday with donated funds.

She wormed her way into COPE, stealing the limelight and raising funds for their causes, but the money never reached the political party or their benefactors. “She has to be stopped”, says Francois Malan. “The public funds her, thinking it’s for a good cause, but it could not be further from the truth”. As a member of the executive of COPE, he should know. He introduced her to Lekota, the party leader, only to see her hijack their community initiatives for personal gain. “She embarrassed us”, he says.





Further information:
Els prays on people's emotions and good nature and needs to be stopped!
During Lockdown she was involved with a scuffle with the police on a CT beach. She claimed she was beaten and broke her back. To this day she says she is wheelchair bound even though she lives on the fourth floor of an apartment building with no lifts. She raised money for medical expenses but doctors' reports say there is nothing wrong with her.


To tell this story we will interview the following people:
Hanlie – she has a file on Debbie and has investigated some of her claims. She has proof that Debbie falsified her medical records when she claimed that she broke her back. She is also in contact with donors who helped Debbie financially and now regret ever doing it.
Hanlie lives in Rustenburg (082 471 3501)
Francois – he is a high ranking member of Cope and has many stories to tell about their dealing with Debbie. In the end they had to publicly distance themselves from Debbie.
Francois is Cape Town based. (078 370 9633)
Gardner – he dated Debbie and when the relationship went sour, Debbie accused him of rape and the sexual abuse of their child. He also has stories of how Debbie took money from artists and sponsors for concerts which never happened. Venues and artists were never paid.
Gardner is Cape Town based. (061 840 9754)
Tanya Muller – she is a lawyer and also the CEO of a non-profit organization. She understands the laws regulating donations and is of the opinion that what Debbie does is completely illegal and punishable by law.
Tanya is Pretoria based. (072 082 6620)

Extra Budget Items:
Travel to CT and car hire to shoot the second leg of the insert.

Press Release:


Trick or Treat?
She appears on the frontlines as the champion of several underdog causes. From assisting drought-stricken farmers, to protesting for human rights – she uses highly charged campaigns to entice her dedicated followers to open their hearts and their wallets. Now, Carte Blanche investigates claims that Debbie Els is in fact a serial opportunist, milking the limelight and people's good intentions for her own personal gain.
Producer: Stenette Grosskopf | Presenter: Derek Watts
Watch the trailer

Script:


DEBBIE ELS – SCRIPT
V/O
Our country faces many challenges – like crime, violence and corruption. But fortunately there are selfless people dedicating their lives to fighting for what’s important.
LINK
One woman has made it her mission to protect South Africa – from Covid, lockdown, gender-based violence, farm murders and of course gun laws… and everything in-between. She’s led protests around the country and even campaigned some issues abroad. …
V/O
Her name is Debbie Els.
UPSOUND
The women in our country are being raped and murdered…
V/O
But some online research leaves a nagging feeling that things aren’t what they seem. So, we head to Rustenburg in the North West on a quest for the truth. It’s here that we meet a retired police captain using her considerable investigative skills to unmask the real Debbie.
Hanlie
Derek: When did you first hear about Debbie Els?

Met die Brendon Horner moord, die optog in Senekal was sy baie betrokke en het baie live uitsendings gemaak op facebook, en dan gee sy voor asof sy nou verslag doen en weet wat daar aangaan.
V/O
And followers from across the world tune in to her live social media feeds for news about the latest campaigns and causes…
UPSOUND
Hi People I’m coming up just to give you a bit of an update…
Hanlie
Members wat sy kan bereik op haar platforms is omtrent 130 000…


V/O
Hanlie Nel spent 22 years in the police service, and says she knows a scam when she sees one…
Hanlie
Sy’s skaamteloos, sy doen dit skaamteloos…
Derek: But it doesn’t really affect you?
Dit doen. Dit pla my. Sy manipuleer mense. Sy jok vir hulle om geld te kry…
V/O
Hanlie launched her investigation after an anti-lockdown protest in Cape Town last year made the news. Debbie and some fellow protesters were involved in a tussle with the police.
Hanlie
Toe het sy beweer dat die polisie haar aangerand het en uit die videos wat hulle geplaas het en wat hulle die wêreld ingestuur het was dit vir my duidelik hulle hierdie polisie uitgelok…
UPSOUND VID
Gender Based Violence. If the president doesn’t do something about these police, okay, we will not stop until they are being dealt with. And you have a lawsuit that is going to skrik for nothing coming your way. You will pay for what you’ve done to me. I have to sit up straight now. I can’t lay down, I can’t hardly walk. I’m wearing a brace…
V/O
Debbie apparently laid charges against the officers and, in the weeks that followed, shared details online about her injuries…
Hanlie
Ek het gehoor dat Debbie beweer het sy het haar rug gebreek.
UPSOUND
The L1, L2 and a leaking L4…

My Hip might be fractured.


V/O
Within days of the incident Debbie was apparently wheelchair-bound…
Hanlie
Sy het op ‘n stadium het sy haar medical records gewys maar sy wys net die deeltjies wat haar storie support.
V/O
Hanlie worked meticulously: using screenshots from Debbie’s facebook feeds she carefully put together the pieces of the puzzle, eventually finding evidence that tell a very different story…
Hanlie
Wat sy het is iets van osteoperose en van bene wat verbrokkel – dit het niks te doen met die polisie wat jou rug gebreek het nie.
V/O
But, it seems, being confined to a wheelchair hasn’t slowed Debbie down.
UPSOUND
They’ve also torn my meniscus, my knee… and I got a death sentence on the 9th of October…
V/O
The “Death Sentence” Debbie is referring to … is when doctors supposedly found evidence of lung cancer during the original CT scan to check out her spine injuries…
Debbie
Yes they found a mass, a very large mass in my left lung. They think it’s in my bones already. They’ve also said that I might have leukemia.

It’s now in my right lung, and I’ve got lumps under my arms….
V/O
Information about a person’s medical condition is confidencial, but Carte Blanche has decided to share some details because it is in the public interest.

The mass in her upper left lung is reportedly smoking-related emphysema – and she had an infection which improved somewhat by the end of November….

Debbie’s GP has confirmed all the injuries and cancers, … and yet there is no mention of “cancer” on the documents we’ve seen.
LINK
With Debbie Els supporting so many causes and her exorbitant medical bills on top of that people are graciously opening their wallets offering financial support from across the globe.
V/O
According to an online fundraising page, she successfully raised over R26,000 in 2021… And that’s just one campaign! …
Hanlie
Van dag een af, het hulle op haar facebook groep vir donasies gevra want sy het nie ‘n medies nie en sy wil nie graag staatshospitaal toe gaan nie…
V/O
Yet it appears that Debbie’s examinations and scans were done at Cape Town’s Karl Bremer State Hospital.
Hanlie
Derek: How much do you think she collected in donations for her medical expenses?

Ek het nou nie toegang tot haar bankrekening nie, maar sy het vir baie mense bedank.
UPSOUND
I thank you all for everything that you’ve done ….
UPSOUND

There are some people that don’t believe what I say. So, I just want to show you… My one lot of medication, like you can see, is R1291.52
V/O
Hanlie managed to get sight of the original prescription and that amount is in fact for weight-loss injections, for Debbie’s daughter…
V/O
Keen to hear her side of the story, while still in Rustenburg, we called to set up an appointment with Debbie.
UPSOUND
That’s confirmed. 2:30 tomorrow in Cape Town at your location.
Yes.
V/O
Within 5 minutes her lawyer, Tamara Victor called me back.
Tamara Victor
Derek, I have a few questions as my client’s legal representative about the story that you want to do tomorrow…
V/O
After answering her questions, Victor said she needed to confer with her client.
Tamara Victor
I’ll give you a call back. Is that okay?

That’s fine, you can speak to me or our producer…
V/O
And though that call never came, we headed to the Mother City early the next morning…
UPSOUND
Next stop… Cape Town
V/O
To fully appreciate the Debbie Els story, we need to venture back in time. Before her social activism she was manager to the stars. According to various sources, Debbie had big dreams that seldom became a reality. And, when money did come in, it rarely made it to the artists themselves.
V/O
Francois Malan is a senior member of the Congress of the People. We meet in the gardens at Parliament. He too has a history with Debbie Els.
Francois
When you meet somebody for the first time you never know who you meet until you walk a path with someone.
V/O
Debbie also made an impression on party leader, Mosiuoa Lekota, and they welcomed her with open arms.
Francois
Debbie requested to become part of COPE and at that stage she became part of the furniture of COPE, yes…
V/O
Then Debbie came up with the idea of making a movie to highlight the plight of the country’s farmers, apparently even writing the screenplay herself.
We had some questions about Francois’s role in the scheme, and put them to him in an online chat a few days later…
Francois
I thought it was not a bad idea to showcase the current atrocities …
V/O
Debbie’s plan included a marketing video - news interview-style – in which Francois would ask the questions and she would explain the movie’s purpose.
Francois
I never saw the script though, I must say, I didn’t think about asking for evidence of the script because there was no reason to doubt. And she was convincing!
V/O
Despite assistance, donations and a trip to the USA, the movie never materialized… and Francois started doubting her intentions.
He recalls an incident at parliament where Debbie had a fleeting encounter with former DA leader, Musi Maimane… She insisted Malan take a photo of them.
Francois
She posts this saying look here I’ve spoken to Maimane, we’re going to have meetings, blah, blah, blah…. She uses every opportunity she can get.
V/O
She even aspired to becoming part of COPE’s leadership, but then Francois got his hands on some eye-opening information.
Francois
I received intel that was on social media. Allegations of doing gigs, arranging talent, arranging artists to come, and then doing the gigs and not getting paid. And the people asking where is my money?
V/O
COPE’s public image was at risk, and Debbie was asked to walk away, but she didn’t leave the limelight…
UPSOUND:
Now I am here for the farmers…


V/O
Back in Cape Town, there’s still no word from Debbie or her lawyer, so we head into the suburbs hoping to meet her face-to-face…
DEREK LINK
So Debbie agreed to an appointment this afternoon. Tamara said she would confirm it in a matter of minutes… It’s more than 20 hours later… So, we’ve flown down to Cape Town to meet Debbie Els.
V/O
And after all that we’re told that Debbie moved out some time ago. So it’s another call to her lawyer, Tamara Victor….


UPSOUND Tamara
Well Debbie wasn’t… uhm she isn’t very well. I thought that you got the voicenote, that’s why I didn’t phone you again…

Derek: You sent it to this number?

Yes, yes..
V/O
But we have no record of having received a voice note.
UPSOUND
Tamara

Derek: Is she still in a wheelchair?

Yes, she’s still in a wheelchair. She’s mostly seated and she’s going for a lot of treatment at the moment.
V/O
Interestingly, Debbie was strong enough to do an online interview the very next day… Again, she described all her medical conditions…
UPSOUND Debbie Els
It’s my choice not to take Chemo… It’s my choice not to have the back operation they wanted me to have, the spinal operation… It’s my choice, it’s my body…
V/O
Instead, Debbie has opted for alternative treatment at a clinic in Cape Town…
Hanlie
Dit is soos ‘n detox. Ek het die hele treatment-proses ook uitgevind


V/O
The Clinic is nowhere to be found on the internet, but Hanlie Nel managed to get a copy of an invoice for some of Debbie’s treatments. There is no practice number on the invoice, no phone number… and her treatment is simply listed as a 6-day Combo Detox Treatment charged at R8,000.
Hanlie
Ek het 'n probleem dat sy ook vir die mense beweer dat hierdie alternative treatment het 'n 100% slaagsyfer ….


V/O
Hanlie laid fraud charges against Debbie late last year, and the investigation is ongoing. Meanwhile, rumours of our investigation this week fired up Debbie’s die-hard supporters and her lawyer sent a letter saying that her client is, quote: “vehemently opposed to the allegations” …


Hanlie
Derek: What would you like to see happen here?

Sy moet stop. Sy moet stop om mense uit te buit en om mense te manipuleer







PROMO 1 11”
A self-styled Good Samaritan is allegedly using emotive causes to entice followers to open their wallets – but is she legitimate or using the limelight for her own personal gain?




PROMO 2 21”
She’s a social activist at the forefront of petitioning for human rights and freedom of choice, and before that she was manager to the stars!

UPSOUND… Francois not paying

Now she’s claiming to have paid the ultimate price for her crusade… We search for what’s true and what’s not….




PROMO 3 21”
Gender-based violence, farm murders and even gun laws…

These emotive issues have placed her in the limelight…

UPSOUND

But is she leading her followers down the garden path?

Producer: Stenette Grosskopf | Presenter: Derek Watts Watch the trailer Script: DEBBIE ELS – SCRIPT V/O Our country faces many challenges – like crime, violence and corruption. But fortunately there are selfless people dedicating their lives to fighting for what’s important. LINK One woman has made it her mission to protect South Africa – from Covid, lockdown, gender-based violence, farm murders and of course gun laws… and everything in-between. She’s led protests around the country and even campaigned some issues abroad. … V/O Her name is Debbie Els. UPSOUND The women in our country are being raped and murdered… V/O But some online research leaves a nagging feeling that things aren’t what they seem. So, we head to Rustenburg in the North West on a quest for the truth. It’s here that we meet a retired police captain using her considerable investigative skills to unmask the real Debbie. Hanlie Derek: When did you first hear about Debbie Els? Met die Brendon Horner moord, die optog in Senekal was sy baie betrokke en het baie live uitsendings gemaak op facebook, en dan gee sy voor asof sy nou verslag doen en weet wat daar aangaan. V/O And followers from across the world tune in to her live social media feeds for news about the latest campaigns and causes… UPSOUND Hi People I’m coming up just to give you a bit of an update… Hanlie Members wat sy kan bereik op haar platforms is omtrent 130 000… V/O Hanlie Nel spent 22 years in the police service, and says she knows a scam when she sees one… Hanlie Sy’s skaamteloos, sy doen dit skaamteloos… Derek: But it doesn’t really affect you? Dit doen. Dit pla my. Sy manipuleer mense. Sy jok vir hulle om geld te kry… V/O Hanlie launched her investigation after an anti-lockdown protest in Cape Town last year made the news. Debbie and some fellow protesters were involved in a tussle with the police. Hanlie Toe het sy beweer dat die polisie haar aangerand het en uit die videos wat hulle geplaas het en wat hulle die wêreld ingestuur het was dit vir my duidelik hulle hierdie polisie uitgelok… UPSOUND VID Gender Based Violence. If the president doesn’t do something about these police, okay, we will not stop until they are being dealt with. And you have a lawsuit that is going to skrik for nothing coming your way. You will pay for what you’ve done to me. I have to sit up straight now. I can’t lay down, I can’t hardly walk. I’m wearing a brace… V/O Debbie apparently laid charges against the officers and, in the weeks that followed, shared details online about her injuries… Hanlie Ek het gehoor dat Debbie beweer het sy het haar rug gebreek. UPSOUND The L1, L2 and a leaking L4… My Hip might be fractured. V/O Within days of the incident Debbie was apparently wheelchair-bound… Hanlie Sy het op ‘n stadium het sy haar medical records gewys maar sy wys net die deeltjies wat haar storie support. V/O Hanlie worked meticulously: using screenshots from Debbie’s facebook feeds she carefully put together the pieces of the puzzle, eventually finding evidence that tell a very different story… Hanlie Wat sy het is iets van osteoperose en van bene wat verbrokkel – dit het niks te doen met die polisie wat jou rug gebreek het nie. V/O But, it seems, being confined to a wheelchair hasn’t slowed Debbie down. UPSOUND They’ve also torn my meniscus, my knee… and I got a death sentence on the 9th of October… V/O The “Death Sentence” Debbie is referring to … is when doctors supposedly found evidence of lung cancer during the original CT scan to check out her spine injuries… Debbie Yes they found a mass, a very large mass in my left lung. They think it’s in my bones already. They’ve also said that I might have leukemia. It’s now in my right lung, and I’ve got lumps under my arms…. V/O Information about a person’s medical condition is confidencial, but Carte Blanche has decided to share some details because it is in the public interest. The mass in her upper left lung is reportedly smoking-related emphysema – and she had an infection which improved somewhat by the end of November…. Debbie’s GP has confirmed all the injuries and cancers, … and yet there is no mention of “cancer” on the documents we’ve seen. LINK With Debbie Els supporting so many causes and her exorbitant medical bills on top of that people are graciously opening their wallets offering financial support from across the globe. V/O According to an online fundraising page, she successfully raised over R26,000 in 2021… And that’s just one campaign! … Hanlie Van dag een af, het hulle op haar facebook groep vir donasies gevra want sy het nie ‘n medies nie en sy wil nie graag staatshospitaal toe gaan nie… V/O Yet it appears that Debbie’s examinations and scans were done at Cape Town’s Karl Bremer State Hospital. Hanlie Derek: How much do you think she collected in donations for her medical expenses? Ek het nou nie toegang tot haar bankrekening nie, maar sy het vir baie mense bedank. UPSOUND I thank you all for everything that you’ve done …. UPSOUND There are some people that don’t believe what I say. So, I just want to show you… My one lot of medication, like you can see, is R1291.52 V/O Hanlie managed to get sight of the original prescription and that amount is in fact for weight-loss injections, for Debbie’s daughter… V/O Keen to hear her side of the story, while still in Rustenburg, we called to set up an appointment with Debbie. UPSOUND That’s confirmed. 2:30 tomorrow in Cape Town at your location. Yes. V/O Within 5 minutes her lawyer, Tamara Victor called me back. Tamara Victor Derek, I have a few questions as my client’s legal representative about the story that you want to do tomorrow… V/O After answering her questions, Victor said she needed to confer with her client. Tamara Victor I’ll give you a call back. Is that okay? That’s fine, you can speak to me or our producer… V/O And though that call never came, we headed to the Mother City early the next morning… UPSOUND Next stop… Cape Town V/O To fully appreciate the Debbie Els story, we need to venture back in time. Before her social activism she was manager to the stars. According to various sources, Debbie had big dreams that seldom became a reality. And, when money did come in, it rarely made it to the artists themselves. V/O Francois Malan is a senior member of the Congress of the People. We meet in the gardens at Parliament. He too has a history with Debbie Els. Francois When you meet somebody for the first time you never know who you meet until you walk a path with someone. V/O Debbie also made an impression on party leader, Mosiuoa Lekota, and they welcomed her with open arms. Francois Debbie requested to become part of COPE and at that stage she became part of the furniture of COPE, yes… V/O Then Debbie came up with the idea of making a movie to highlight the plight of the country’s farmers, apparently even writing the screenplay herself. We had some questions about Francois’s role in the scheme, and put them to him in an online chat a few days later… Francois I thought it was not a bad idea to showcase the current atrocities … V/O Debbie’s plan included a marketing video - news interview-style – in which Francois would ask the questions and she would explain the movie’s purpose. Francois I never saw the script though, I must say, I didn’t think about asking for evidence of the script because there was no reason to doubt. And she was convincing! V/O Despite assistance, donations and a trip to the USA, the movie never materialized… and Francois started doubting her intentions. He recalls an incident at parliament where Debbie had a fleeting encounter with former DA leader, Musi Maimane… She insisted Malan take a photo of them. Francois She posts this saying look here I’ve spoken to Maimane, we’re going to have meetings, blah, blah, blah…. She uses every opportunity she can get. V/O She even aspired to becoming part of COPE’s leadership, but then Francois got his hands on some eye-opening information. Francois I received intel that was on social media. Allegations of doing gigs, arranging talent, arranging artists to come, and then doing the gigs and not getting paid. And the people asking where is my money? V/O COPE’s public image was at risk, and Debbie was asked to walk away, but she didn’t leave the limelight… UPSOUND: Now I am here for the farmers… V/O Back in Cape Town, there’s still no word from Debbie or her lawyer, so we head into the suburbs hoping to meet her face-to-face… DEREK LINK So Debbie agreed to an appointment this afternoon. Tamara said she would confirm it in a matter of minutes… It’s more than 20 hours later… So, we’ve flown down to Cape Town to meet Debbie Els. V/O And after all that we’re told that Debbie moved out some time ago. So it’s another call to her lawyer, Tamara Victor…. UPSOUND Tamara Well Debbie wasn’t… uhm she isn’t very well. I thought that you got the voicenote, that’s why I didn’t phone you again… Derek: You sent it to this number? Yes, yes.. V/O But we have no record of having received a voice note. UPSOUND Tamara Derek: Is she still in a wheelchair? Yes, she’s still in a wheelchair. She’s mostly seated and she’s going for a lot of treatment at the moment. V/O Interestingly, Debbie was strong enough to do an online interview the very next day… Again, she described all her medical conditions… UPSOUND Debbie Els It’s my choice not to take Chemo… It’s my choice not to have the back operation they wanted me to have, the spinal operation… It’s my choice, it’s my body… V/O Instead, Debbie has opted for alternative treatment at a clinic in Cape Town… Hanlie Dit is soos ‘n detox. Ek het die hele treatment-proses ook uitgevind V/O The Clinic is nowhere to be found on the internet, but Hanlie Nel managed to get a copy of an invoice for some of Debbie’s treatments. There is no practice number on the invoice, no phone number… and her treatment is simply listed as a 6-day Combo Detox Treatment charged at R8,000. Hanlie Ek het 'n probleem dat sy ook vir die mense beweer dat hierdie alternative treatment het 'n 100% slaagsyfer …. V/O Hanlie laid fraud charges against Debbie late last year, and the investigation is ongoing. Meanwhile, rumours of our investigation this week fired up Debbie’s die-hard supporters and her lawyer sent a letter saying that her client is, quote: “vehemently opposed to the allegations” … Hanlie Derek: What would you like to see happen here? Sy moet stop. Sy moet stop om mense uit te buit en om mense te manipuleer PROMO 1 11” A self-styled Good Samaritan is allegedly using emotive causes to entice followers to open their wallets – but is she legitimate or using the limelight for her own personal gain? PROMO 2 21” She’s a social activist at the forefront of petitioning for human rights and freedom of choice, and before that she was manager to the stars! UPSOUND… Francois not paying Now she’s claiming to have paid the ultimate price for her crusade… We search for what’s true and what’s not…. PROMO 3 21” Gender-based violence, farm murders and even gun laws… These emotive issues have placed her in the limelight… UPSOUND But is she leading her followers down the garden path?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Online Money scams are nothing new, but Debbie Els has been living off Good Samaritan-donations for many years!
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Debbie Els is a colourful character. When the farmers marched on Senekal, she was in the front line to support them, when parents cordoned off the Brackenfell High School in Cape Town to defend it against EFF protesters, Debbie went live on social media and claimed that she was under attack. She was nowhere near the incident. She picked a fight with the Cape Town Police when they arrested bathers during the Covid lockdown. She claimed afterwards that she was severely beaten and even broke her back in two places. “Rubbish”, says those who know her, “there is nothing wrong, She just loves the limelight”.
metadata.Summary: The name, Debbie Els is linked to numerous Facebook groups raising funds for worthy causes -- they include the Million March and I’m Staying, The plight of Farmers in SA, Anti-Vaxx... you name it. She adopts a cause and proceeds to raise funds via various FB groups.. But the money never gets to the beneficiaries... it ends up in her pocket or spent on unrelated expenses. Els has been in jail twice - for selling properties that did not belong to her, and for illegally marrying a man in Mauritius whilst still legally married to her husband in SA. She has been agent to the stars, arranged concerts and never paying artists and ... She even dated a young up-and-coming Afrikaans artist, but when things turned sour she accused him of rape and child abuse... The cases against him were dropped. Debbie then set her sights on Farm Murders and decided that she would make a movie to highlight the plight of white farmers under attack in SA. She got a script from a young man and never paid him. Then she raised funds to go sell the idea in Hollywood, and although she did go to the USA, there never was a movie and she ended up having nothing more than a holiday with donated funds. She wormed her way into COPE, stealing the limelight and raising funds for their causes, but the money never reached the political party or their benefactors. “She has to be stopped”, says Francois Malan. “The public funds her, thinking it’s for a good cause, but it could not be further from the truth”. As a member of the executive of COPE, he should know. He introduced her to Lekota, the party leader, only to see her hijack their community initiatives for personal gain. “She embarrassed us”, he says.
metadata.Further information: Els prays on people's emotions and good nature and needs to be stopped! During Lockdown she was involved with a scuffle with the police on a CT beach. She claimed she was beaten and broke her back. To this day she says she is wheelchair bound even though she lives on the fourth floor of an apartment building with no lifts. She raised money for medical expenses but doctors' reports say there is nothing wrong with her. To tell this story we will interview the following people: Hanlie – she has a file on Debbie and has investigated some of her claims. She has proof that Debbie falsified her medical records when she claimed that she broke her back. She is also in contact with donors who helped Debbie financially and now regret ever doing it. Hanlie lives in Rustenburg (082 471 3501) Francois – he is a high ranking member of Cope and has many stories to tell about their dealing with Debbie. In the end they had to publicly distance themselves from Debbie. Francois is Cape Town based. (078 370 9633) Gardner – he dated Debbie and when the relationship went sour, Debbie accused him of rape and the sexual abuse of their child. He also has stories of how Debbie took money from artists and sponsors for concerts which never happened. Venues and artists were never paid. Gardner is Cape Town based. (061 840 9754) Tanya Muller – she is a lawyer and also the CEO of a non-profit organization. She understands the laws regulating donations and is of the opinion that what Debbie does is completely illegal and punishable by law. Tanya is Pretoria based. (072 082 6620)
